title: The French Textile Eco-Score: 2026 - Key Updates for Fashion Brands
summary: Deep dive for fashion brands - The French Textile Environmental Cost (ex. Eco-Score) entered into force on 1st October 2025.
body_markdown:
> Status: ✅ Approved law


The French Eco-score, part of the 2021 Climate and Resilience Law, is also known as “environmental labeling” or “affichage environmental” and has been officially renamed to "Environmental Cost" or “cout environmental”.


The Ministry of Ecological Transition approved the final texts, and the Environmental Cost entered into force in October 2025. Ecobalyse – France's official environmental cost calculator – is the reference methodology for calculating the score.


The next important deadline is October 2026. From that date, any third party – retailers, NGOs, comparison platforms – can publish an Environmental Cost score on behalf of a brand, without the brand's prior approval, using conservative data assumptions.


If your apparel company, whether French or foreign, operates within the French market, calculating the score yourself becomes crucial to staying competitive. This article covers what you need to know to comply.


Let’s dive into all the details or watch this 15-minute crash course:


Find the[French version](https://www.carbonfact.com/fr/blog/eco-score-textile) of this article here 🇫🇷 Read more about our[Eco-Score Software](https://www.carbonfact.com/eco-score-software-textile) for Textile and Fashion.


#### TL;DR


-


What:


French Eco-score, part of the 2021 Climate and Resilience Law. Assigns a single environmental score (Environmental Cost) to textile products sold in France.


- Who:


Applies to all producers, importers, and distributors placing textile products on the French market, regardless of country of origin.


- When:


From October 2025, the voluntary display phase begins (only brands may publish scores). From October 2026, third parties may publish scores if brands have not. Environmental Cost becomes mandatory if another environmental score is shown.


## What is the French Eco-Score?


The French ‘Environmental Cost’ (French: Coût Environnemental), is part of France’s affichage environnemental (environmental labeling) scheme for textiles, introduced under the AGEC law and formalized by the 2021 Climate and Resilience Law. It is a methodology developed under the French government’s environmental labelling program, coordinated with ADEME (French Agency for Ecological Transition), to assign a single score (in environmental points) to the impacts of textile products in France.


This methodology for assessing and communicating the environmental impacts of textile products is based on[life cycle assessment](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/knowledge/lca-fashion-textile) (LCA) and evaluates 16 environmental indicators. Each indicator is normalized and weighted according to the official methodology.


The weighted results are summed, and additional parameters such as durability and microfiber release are added to produce the final score in environmental points, which is displayed on a consumer-facing textile label. The higher the score, the bigger the environmental impact the product has.
